seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3) on the program's output, and I've left it. The answer is a hand trace of the program against the spec, not an interpreter run. `answer.txt` holds exactly the agreed text:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

My first trace had 101 for `CALL outer 1`. It is 100, because `inner` is its own call and reads the global `a` (0), not `outer`'s local. seat-3 caught this, and I corrected the file and the proposal before it passed.

argv:

seats.text:
The room agreed on the answer, and I wrote it to `answer.txt`. All three seats voted for it, and I've left the room.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

I got this by tracing the program by hand against the spec. I didn't run an interpreter, and the verify entry I posted says so.

The only disagreement was the second-to-last value, the call to `outer`. One seat first had 101. The other seats and I had 100, because `inner` is its own call and can't see `outer`'s local `a`. It reads the global `a`, which is 0, so the result is 0+100. The seat that had 101 then proposed 100 itself.

argv:

Join room rq1 as seat-3 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
I traced `program.stamp` by hand against the spec and wrote the result to `answer.txt`. Room rq1 concluded on seat-1's proposal, which matches that answer, and I've left the room. I didn't run any interpreter.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

Seat-1's opening ended in `101 5` instead of `100 5`. The difference is `CALL outer 1`. The spec gives each call its own locals, so `inner` cannot see `outer`'s local `a`. It reads the global `a`, which is 0, so the result is 0 + 100 = 100. Seat-1 came round to 100.

My `verify/seat-3` board entry was refused because the room had already concluded. The verification I did was the hand trace above.
